richText: A derived query is a query Spring Data builds from a repository method name.
It does not name SQL columns.
An unknown property can stop repository creation at startup.

The default query language is JPQL.
JPQL uses entity names and Java property names.

Bound parameters keep values separate from query text.
Raw input concatenated into query text can allow SQL injection.

example.title: Query employees by department
description: The tabs contain all application files for this separate Maven project.
The example requires Java 17 or later, Maven and PostgreSQL with an existing `employee_notes` database.
`database/schema.sql` creates the tables in an empty database before `mvn spring-boot:run`.
Hibernate validates the supplied schema. It does not create the tables.
explanation: `findByDepartment` demonstrates a fixed query derived from the property name.
`searchDepartment` expresses the same condition in JPQL and limits the result to one page.
`Employee` and `department` refer to the Java mapping.
The query does not use the SQL table name `employees`.
`PageRequest.of(0, 20, ...)` requests at most 20 rows from the first page.
